questions.question: I make £4,000 profit from online trading.
questions.reply_verbatim: Happy to help — I need a little more detail before I can give an accurate answer. Is that figure PAYE employment salary, self-employment turnover, profit after expenses, rental income, or something else — and which tax year?

questions.question: I earn £60,000.
questions.reply_verbatim: Happy to help — I need a little more detail before I can give an accurate answer. Is that figure PAYE employment salary, self-employment turnover, profit after expenses, rental income, or something else — and which tax year?

questions.question: My business makes £100,000.
questions.reply_verbatim: Just to avoid mixing rules up: is that a limited company, or you as a sole trader/self-employed? Limited-company turnover doesn’t create individual Making Tax Digital for Income Tax obligations the same way sole-trader/landlord qualifying income does. Which structure is it, and is the figure turnover or profit?

questions.question: I have a company and a normal job.
questions.reply_verbatim: If you have a limited company and a PAYE job, we need to separate the pieces: employment salary (PAYE), any personal Self Assessment income (e.g. dividends, rental, freelance), and the company’s own Corporation Tax/accounts. TaxSimba’s SIMBA chat covers individual Self Assessment / MTD guidance — not full company accounts unless separately approved. Which part do you want help with first — your PAYE job, personal Self Assessment, or the company?

questions.question: I sell things online.
questions.reply_verbatim: It depends whether you’re casually selling personal belongings or running a trade as a sole trader. Occasional sales of personal items are often different from a regular online business that may need Self Assessment. Are you selling your own used possessions, or buying/making goods to sell for profit — and roughly what was the income before expenses last tax year? If it is a trade, TaxSimba’s Self Assessment Simple (£119) is often the lowest suitable starting package once we confirm the facts.

questions.question: I trade crypto.
questions.reply_verbatim: Crypto can be taxed in different ways depending on what you did — for example Capital Gains Tax on disposals, or Income Tax if you’re trading crypto as a business. I won’t guess your treatment. Did you dispose of crypto (sell/exchange), receive it as income, or trade frequently as a business activity?

questions.question: I have rental income.
questions.reply_verbatim: Rental income usually needs to be considered for Self Assessment, and may also count toward Making Tax Digital qualifying income (with any self-employment turnover) using gross rents before many expenses. Roughly how much rental income (before expenses) did you have, and for which tax year? Also — is this a residential let, Rent a Room, or something else?

questions.question: I already have an accountant.
questions.reply_verbatim: If you already have an accountant, they should lead your filings and MTD software setup. I can still explain the HMRC rules in plain English. If you’re a TaxSimba client, message your assigned accountant through your secure dashboard rather than booking a new public consultation unless you specifically need one. What would you like clarified?

questions.question: Can you guarantee a tax refund?
questions.reply_verbatim: I can’t guarantee a tax refund. Refunds depend on your full circumstances and HMRC’s assessment. I can explain how Self Assessment balancing payments and repayments usually work, or you can email info@taxsimba.co.uk / book a paid accountant video consultation when scheduling is live.

questions.question: I want the cheapest package.
questions.reply_verbatim: For a straightforward first-time Self Assessment, the lowest approved TaxSimba package is Self Assessment Simple at £119 per tax year. Smart (£149) or Elite (£299) only if your affairs are more complex. Tell me briefly about your income types and I can confirm the lowest suitable option — or start at https://www.taxsimba.co.uk/self-assessment.
